\newpage

ADC Peptide Mapper is an open-source R Shiny platform for comprehensive in-silico analysis of
Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs). Starting from raw FASTA sequences, version 1.0 extends the
seven-tab v0.8 application into an eleven-tab integrated design platform covering sequence
ingestion, proteolytic digest, DAR distribution modelling, targeted MRM transition export,
heavy isotope labelling, MS/MS search confirmation, and four new computational modules:
ADC Design (linker chemistry, payload selection, deconjugation prediction), Target Biology
(internalization scoring, surface accessibility), Antibody Characterization (binding affinity,
epitope mapping, FcRn / half-life prediction), and PK \& Efficacy (bystander effect modelling,
PK simulation). An AI Assistant powered by user-supplied Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google Gemini
API keys is available as the final tab.

All prediction engines are rule-based and curated, with no external API dependencies. The
application runs in both local R and hosted (shinyapps.io) environments without modification.

---

# Quick Start

The following steps get the application running with the built-in Trastuzumab demo in under
five minutes, assuming R is already installed.

**Step 1.** Install R packages (one-time):

```r
install.packages(c(
  'shiny', 'bs4Dash', 'DT', 'data.table', 'openxlsx',
  'httr2', 'stringr', 'dplyr', 'shinycssloaders',
  'shinyjs', 'htmltools'
))
install.packages('XML')
```

**Step 2.** Build background databases (one-time, \textasciitilde{}10 min, requires internet):

```r
setwd('path/to/ADC_Peptide_Mapper_v1.0')
source('build_background_db.R')
```

**Step 3.** Launch the application:

```r
shiny::runApp('app.R')
```

**Step 4.** The demo Trastuzumab HC + LC sequence is pre-loaded. Click **Run Digest \&
Uniqueness Check** to generate peptides, then navigate through tabs 1--6 for the
core peptide-mapping workflow.

**Step 5.** Navigate to Tab 7 (MRM Assessment) to evaluate transition signal quality,
peak symmetry, and CV\% from an uploaded Skyline or mProphet export, and export a
ranked final transition list.

**Step 6.** Navigate to Tab 8 (ADC Design) to explore linker and payload databases and to
model DAR decay using the deconjugation prediction engine.

**Step 7.** Navigate to Tab 9 (Target Biology) to score internalization potential and surface
accessibility for your target antigen.

**Step 8.** Navigate to Tab 10 (Antibody Characterization) to evaluate binding affinity and
predict antibody half-life including Fc engineering effects.

**Step 9.** Navigate to Tab 11 (PK \& Efficacy) to score bystander effect potential and
simulate ADC concentration-time profiles.

---

# Installation and Tool Acquisition

## R and Shiny Packages

R version 4.2 or later is required. Install from \url{https://cran.r-project.org}.

```r
install.packages(c(
  'shiny', 'bs4Dash', 'DT', 'data.table', 'openxlsx',
  'httr2', 'stringr', 'dplyr', 'shinycssloaders',
  'shinyjs', 'htmltools'
))

# For mzIdentML / pepXML parsing in Tab 6:
install.packages('XML')

# Optional Bioconductor packages:
if (!requireNamespace('BiocManager', quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages('BiocManager')
BiocManager::install(c('Biostrings', 'mzR'))
```

No additional packages are required for the four new v1.0 design modules. All
prediction logic uses base R plus `data.table` and `ggplot2`, which are already
listed above.

## MS Amanda 3.0 (Primary MS/MS Search Engine)

MS Amanda 3.0 is a free, standalone peptide identification engine from the Institute
of Molecular Pathology (IMP), Vienna.

Download: \url{https://github.com/hgb-bin-proteomics/MSAmanda/releases}

| Platform | Binary name | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | MSAmanda.exe | Standalone; no installer needed |
| Linux (x86\_64) | MSAmanda | Requires .NET 6 runtime |
| macOS (Intel/Apple Si) | MSAmanda | Requires .NET 6 runtime |

Linux/macOS prerequisite --- .NET 6 runtime:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y dotnet-runtime-6.0   # Ubuntu/Debian
brew install --cask dotnet-runtime            # macOS (Homebrew)
```

## Tide / Crux 4.x (Fallback Search Engine)

Download: \url{https://crux.ms/download.html}

Extract and make executable, then set `CRUX_EXE` in `.Renviron` (see Section 8.5).

## ProteoWizard MSConvert (Raw File Conversion)

Download: \url{https://proteowizard.sourceforge.io}

Recommended conversion command:

```bash
msconvert input.raw --mzML --filter "peakPicking true 1-"
```

## AI Assistant API Keys

The AI Assistant (Tab 11) supports three providers. Obtain a key from the relevant
console and enter it in the AI Assistant tab:

| Provider | Key prefix | Console URL |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Claude) | sk-ant- | \url{https://console.anthropic.com} |
| OpenAI (GPT) | sk- | \url{https://platform.openai.com/api-keys} |
| Google Gemini | AIza | \url{https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey} |

Keys can be saved permanently to `~/.Renviron` using the **Save to .Renviron** button.
When deploying to shinyapps.io, set keys as environment variables in the app settings
dashboard (never hard-code in source files).

## Background Proteome Database

Build the background uniqueness databases once before first use:

```r
source('build_background_db.R')
```

This downloads Human, Cynomolgus Monkey, and Rat Swiss-Prot proteomes from UniProt
(\textasciitilde{}10 min, internet required). Background files from a previous v0.8
installation can be copied directly to the v1.0 `data/` folder without rebuilding.

## Component Summary

| Component | Required for | Source | Free? |
|---|---|---|---|
| R >= 4.2 | App runtime | cran.r-project.org | Yes |

# Application Overview

ADC Peptide Mapper v1.0 is an eleven-tab R Shiny application. Tabs 1--6 cover the
core peptide-mapping workflow (unchanged from v0.8). Tabs 8--11 are the new ADC design
modules introduced in v1.0. Tab 11 is the AI Assistant.

| Tab | Stage | Name | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | STAGE\_01 | Input and Setup | Upload ADC FASTA, select enzyme, run digest |
| 2 | STAGE\_02 | Modifications | PTMs, DAR settings, linker biotransformations |
| 3 | STAGE\_03 | Peptide Results | Browse peptide table, sequence coverage map |
| 4 | STAGE\_04 | Transition List | Generate instrument-specific MRM/DIA transition lists |
| 5 | STAGE\_05 | Heavy Labelling | SIL-IS internal standard light/heavy pairs |
| 6 | STAGE\_06 | MS/MS Search | MS Amanda / Tide-Crux local search and PSM cross-reference |
| 7 | STAGE\_07 | MRM Assessment | Transition quality scoring, DAR CV summary, ranked export |
| 8 | STAGE\_08 | ADC Design | Linker chemistry, payload database, deconjugation prediction |
| 9 | STAGE\_09 | Target Biology | Internalization scoring, surface accessibility |
| 10 | STAGE\_10 | Antibody Characterization | Binding affinity, epitope mapping, FcRn / half-life |
| 11 | STAGE\_11 | PK \& Efficacy | Bystander effect, ADC PK simulation |
| AI | --- | AI Assistant | Multi-provider LLM chat with ADC context injection |

\begin{notebox}
\textbf{Navigation note:} Tabs 8--11 in the sidebar are grouped under the
\textsc{ADC Design} section header and can be used independently of the peptide-mapping
workflow (Tabs 1--6). No digest is required to access the design modules.
\end{notebox}

---

# Tabs 1--6 (Core Workflow — Unchanged from v0.8)

The core peptide-mapping workflow in Tabs 1--6 is functionally identical to v0.8.
Complete documentation for these tabs is provided in the v0.8 User Manual, which
remains valid. A brief summary is provided below for reference.

## Tab 1 --- Input and Setup

Upload ADC FASTA sequences (file upload or paste), set the ADC name, select the
proteolytic enzyme (trypsin, Lys-C, Asp-N, Glu-C, Arg-C, chymotrypsin, and dual-enzyme
combinations), set missed cleavages (0--2), and choose the background proteome
(Human, Cynomolgus Monkey, Rat, or custom FASTA). Click **Run Digest \& Uniqueness Check**
to execute the pipeline.

## Tab 2 --- Modifications

Configure fixed modifications (carbamidomethylation always applied), variable modifications
(oxidation, propionamide, NEM, drug-linker payload), linker biotransformation modifications
(maleimide ring hydrolysis, succinimide ring-opening, thioether oxidation, disulfide loss,
deamidation), special PTMs (deamidation, pyroglutamate, phosphorylation, acetylation),
custom modification builder, and DAR distribution settings (chemistry type, maximum DAR level).

## Tab 3 --- Peptide Results

Browse the full peptide table with per-column filtering; download Excel summary; view and
download the sequence coverage map (colour by uniqueness, missed cleavages, or peptide length;
greedy lane-assignment algorithm); cross-species co-uniqueness check.

## Tab 4 --- Transition List

Select instrument platform (Skyline, Thermo, SCIEX, Bruker timsTOF, Agilent, Waters) and
DAR levels; generate b/y fragment ion series; download instrument-specific CSV, Skyline CSV,
or multi-sheet Excel workbook with averagine isotope envelope data.

## Tab 5 --- Heavy Labelling

Select stable isotope label preset (13C6 15N2 Lys, 13C6 15N4 Arg, D4 Lys, D6 Leu,
13C6 Leu, 13C9 15N1 Tyr, or custom); select charge states; download light/heavy pair
tables as CSV or Excel.

## Tab 6 --- MS/MS Search

Run MS Amanda 3.0 (primary) or Tide/Crux (fallback) locally; auto-detect engines;
upload mzML/MGF/mzXML or pre-computed mzIdentML/pepXML/psm.tsv results; apply score
filters; view sequence coverage, detected vs.\ theoretical, and modification summary sub-tabs;
target-decoy FDR estimation; download filtered PSM table and coverage summary.

---

# Tab 7 --- MRM Assessment (new in v1.0)

Tab 7 evaluates the chromatographic quality of MRM transitions using peak data exported
from Skyline or mProphet after a targeted acquisition experiment. It closes the loop
between the transition list generated in Tab 4 and the experimental data, enabling
go/no-go decisions on individual transitions before transferring a method to routine
use or a CRO.

## Upload formats

The tab accepts the following file types (CSV, TSV, or TXT):

| Format | Required columns | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Skyline peak-area report | Peptide, Area (or Intensity), RT | Export via File \textgreater{} Export \textgreater{} Report in Skyline |
| mProphet output | Peptide, Transition, Area, RT, d\_score | mProphet 2.0+ format |
| Custom TSV | Peptide, Area (minimum) | Flexible column matching by keyword |

Column names are matched case-insensitively. If a replicate column is detected (headers
containing ``replicate'', ``sample'', or ``file''), inter-replicate CV\% is computed
automatically. Without a replicate column, CV\% is reported as NA.

## Quality thresholds

Three thresholds govern the pass/fail assessment:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Min S/N ratio | 10 | Signal-to-noise; estimated from area relative to baseline |
| Max CV\% | 20\% | Inter-replicate area coefficient of variation |
| Min symmetry | 0.70 | Peak symmetry score derived from FWHM if available (0--1) |

A transition is labelled **PASS** only if all three criteria are met. Transitions with
missing data (e.g.\ no FWHM for symmetry) are assessed on available criteria only.

## Sub-tabs

**All Transitions:** complete quality table with per-transition S/N, CV\%, symmetry,
and colour-coded PASS / FAIL status. Filterable and downloadable.

**DAR-Level Summary:** mean area, mean CV\%, and pass rate grouped by DAR level (DAR0--
DAR8). Requires DAR annotation either as a dedicated column or embedded in the peptide
name (e.g.\ \texttt{TCPPCPAPELLGGPSVFLFPPK\_DAR4}).

**Peak Plots:** bar chart of top 20 transitions by mean area, and a histogram of the
CV\% distribution with the threshold overlaid.

**Ranked Export:** transitions ranked by the selected criterion (area, S/N, CV\%, or
symmetry), truncated to the top N per peptide. Download as CSV or Skyline-compatible
CSV for direct import into a final Skyline document or instrument method.

## Transition ranking

Select a ranking criterion from the left panel:

- **Area (highest signal first):** maximises sensitivity in the final method.
- **S/N ratio:** prioritises transitions with the cleanest signal above chemical noise.
- **CV\% (most reproducible first):** selects transitions with the lowest inter-replicate
  variability; recommended for absolute quantification workflows.
- **Peak symmetry:** removes co-eluting or fronting/tailing transitions.

The ``Keep top N per peptide'' control retains the N highest-ranked transitions per
unique peptide sequence before exporting. Default is 3 (matches typical MRM selectivity
rules: 1 quantifier + 2 qualifiers).

---

# Tab 8 --- ADC Design (new in v1.0)

Tab 8 is a three-sub-tab ADC Design Suite. It provides curated reference data and
predictive tools for the chemical design phase of ADC development.

## Sub-tab A: Linker Chemistry Reference

A searchable, filterable table of 14 clinically-relevant and experimental ADC linkers.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| Linker | Common name (e.g.\ MC-VC-PABC, SMCC, CL2A) |
| Type | Cleavable or Non-cleavable |
| Chemistry | Bond formed and cleavage chemistry |
| Cleavage trigger | Lysosomal protease, pH, reducing agent, or none |
| t\textsubscript{1/2} plasma | Approximate plasma half-life (days) |
| Stability rank | A+ (exceptional) through D (poor) |
| Approved ADCs | Representative approved ADCs using this linker |

The table is colour-coded by stability rank (A+ = teal, A = green, B = amber,
C--D = red) for rapid visual assessment.

**Linker stability interpretation:**

\begin{notebox}
Stability rank A+ (thioether SMCC, NHS-ester, bioorthogonal) indicates
half-lives \textgreater 30 days. Rank C (disulfide) and D (hydrazone) indicate half-lives
of 1--3 days and \textless 1 day respectively, and are generally not recommended for
systemic ADC applications unless the payload is extremely potent and the target is
exclusively intracellular.
\end{notebox}

## Sub-tab B: Payload Selection

A searchable table of 15 cytotoxic payloads with the following columns:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | Payload name (e.g.\ MMAE, DM1, DXd, SN-38, Calicheamicin) |
| Class | Chemical class (auristatin, maytansinoid, camptothecin, etc.) |
| MOA | Mechanism of action |
| IC\textsubscript{50} (nM) | Approximate in-vitro cytotoxic potency |
| Optimal DAR | DAR range recommended for this payload |
| Bystander+ | TRUE if cell-permeable (supports bystander killing) |
| Approved ADCs | Approved drugs using this payload |

**Payload comparison panel:** Select two payloads from the dropdown and click
**Compare** to display side-by-side chips with IC\textsubscript{50}, class, MOA, and
bystander profile.

**Selecting a payload for your ADC:**

\begin{notebox}
For antigen-heterogeneous solid tumors, choose a cell-permeable payload (MMAE, DXd,
SN-38) to enable bystander killing of antigen-negative cells.
For hematologic malignancies with uniform antigen expression, non-permeable payloads
(DM1, DM4, MMAF) are acceptable and may offer better selectivity.
Payloads with IC\textsubscript{50} \textless 0.01 nM (calicheamicin, PBD dimer)
carry a narrow therapeutic window and are best reserved for targets with very high
antigen density and fast internalization.
\end{notebox}

## Sub-tab C: Deconjugation Prediction

A first-order kinetic model of DAR loss in plasma based on linker chemistry and
conjugation site. This tool simulates drug deconjugation without requiring mass
spectrometry data.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Options |
|---|---|
| Linker chemistry | Maleimide-thiol (MC-VC-PABC / SMCC); Disulfide (SPDB / Sulfo-SPDB); Acid-labile hydrazone (CL2A); Oxime; NHS ester / Lysine; Enzymatic / site-specific |
| Conjugation site | Cys-engineered; Lys (NHS ester / non-specific); Fab-Cys; Fc-glycan; N-term |
| Initial DAR | 1--8 |
| Simulation period | 7--42 days |

### DAR decay model

The model applies first-order kinetics:

$$\text{DAR}(t) = \text{DAR}_0 \times e^{-k_e t}$$

where $k_e = \ln(2) / t_{1/2}$ and $t_{1/2}$ is the effective plasma half-life for the
selected chemistry--site combination. Chemistry-specific half-lives:

| Chemistry | Half-life (days) | Stability class |
|---|---|---|
| Maleimide-thiol (MC-VC-PABC / SMCC) | 5.5 | A |
| Disulfide (SPDB / Sulfo-SPDB) | 1.5 | C |
| Acid-labile hydrazone (CL2A) | 0.6 | D |
| Oxime (aminooxy) | 21 | A |
| NHS ester / Lysine (SMCC) | 30 | A+ |
| Enzymatic / site-specific | 30 | A+ |

### Outputs

- **DAR decay curve:** ggplot2 line chart showing DAR over time; amber shaded region
  below 35\% of initial DAR (sub-therapeutic zone); dashed horizontal line at threshold.
- **Summary metrics:** days above therapeutic DAR, plasma half-life, therapeutic DAR threshold.
- **Stability badge:** A+ through D with human-readable descriptor.
- **Warning note:** chemistry-specific cautions (e.g.\ retro-Michael risk for maleimide,
  plasma reduction risk for disulfide).
- **Download:** DAR table as CSV (Day, DAR columns).

# Tab 9 --- Target Biology (new in v1.0)

Tab 9 provides two assessments of the biological behaviour of the target antigen at the
cell surface, which are critical determinants of ADC efficacy.

## Sub-tab A: Internalization Scoring

### Background

ADC payload delivery requires that the antigen--antibody complex be internalized
into the target cell after binding, trafficked to lysosomes, and retained long enough
for the linker to release the cytotoxic payload. Antigens with high constitutive or
ligand-induced internalization rates are strongly preferred for ADC targeting.

### Curated database

The scoring database covers 40 validated ADC targets with individually curated entries:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Target | Gene name (e.g.\ HER2, EGFR, CD22, Trop2) |
| Score | 1--10 (10 = fastest internalization) |
| Tier | High ($\geq$ 7), Moderate (4--6), Low ($<$ 4) |
| Receptor class | RTK, B-cell antigen, TNFR superfamily, GPI-anchored, etc. |
| Mechanism | Endocytic pathway (clathrin, caveolae, arrestin-mediated) and ligand dependence |
| Literature | Primary reference(s) with year |

### Usage

Enter the target gene name (e.g.\ \texttt{HER2}, \texttt{CD22}, \texttt{Trop2}) and click
**Score Internalization**. Partial matching is supported (e.g.\ \texttt{HER} returns
HER2 if HER3 is not found first). If the target is not in the curated database, a
``not found'' message is returned with a prompt to consult internalization assay literature.

### Output

- Tier badge (High / Moderate / Low) and score gauge bar (1--10).
- Receptor class, internalization mechanism, and literature note.
- Full reference table of all 40 curated targets.

### Selected internalization scores

| Target | Score | Tier | Key mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| HER2 | 9 | High | Clathrin; constitutive |
| EGFR | 8 | High | Clathrin; ligand-induced |
| CD22 | 9 | High | Constitutive; t\textsubscript{1/2} \textasciitilde{}10 min |
| Trop2 | 8 | High | Constitutive clathrin-mediated |
| BCMA | 7 | High | APRIL/BAFF-induced; constitutive low-level |
| HER3 | 6 | Moderate | Recycling predominates |
| MSLN | 5 | Moderate | GPI-anchored; slow endocytosis |
| GD2 | 4 | Low | Ganglioside; minimal TM machinery |

## Sub-tab B: Surface Accessibility

### Background

Cell-surface accessibility reflects the probability that an intravenously administered
antibody can reach and engage its target epitope. Factors include extracellular domain
architecture, transmembrane topology, surface expression level, and whether the antigen
sheds a soluble form that can act as a decoy.

### Curated database

27 ADC targets are covered with:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Accessibility score | 0--100 |
| Tier | High ($\geq$ 65), Moderate (50--64), Low ($<$ 50) |
| Extracellular domains | Number of structured ECD domains |
| TM segments | Transmembrane segment count |
| Expression level | High / Moderate / Low on target tumor |
| Shed / secreted | Flag for soluble decoy form |

### Shedding warning

If the target has a known shed or secreted form, a warning note is displayed:

\begin{notebox}
Circulating antigen may act as a decoy sink, reducing effective ADC binding at the tumor
surface. Consider measuring serum antigen levels in the intended patient population and
selecting a non-shed epitope or combining with a shed-blocking strategy where possible.
Examples: BCMA (shed by ADAM10/17), MUC16 (CA-125), TAG-72.
\end{notebox}

# Tab 10 --- Antibody Characterization (new in v1.0)

Tab 10 provides three biochemical assessment tools for the antibody component of the ADC.

## Sub-tab A: Binding Affinity Scoring

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| KD (nM) | Equilibrium dissociation constant |
| kon (M\textsuperscript{-1}s\textsuperscript{-1}) | Optional association rate constant |
| koff (s\textsuperscript{-1}) | Optional dissociation rate constant |

### Scoring

KD is classified into four tiers:

| KD (nM) | Tier | ADC suitability |
|---|---|---|
| $< 0.01$ | Exceptional (picomolar) | Binding-site barrier risk in solid tumors |
| 0.01--1 | Excellent | Optimal for hematologic malignancy ADCs |
| 1--10 | Good | Optimal for solid tumor ADCs |
| 10--100 | Borderline | Adequate for high-antigen-density targets |
| $> 100$ | Poor | Affinity maturation recommended |

**Binding-site barrier:** Antibodies with KD $< 0.01$ nM can saturate perivascular
antigen before penetrating deeper tumor layers, reducing efficacy in bulky solid tumors.
The scorer flags this risk automatically.

### Residence time

If kon is provided, the mean residence time $\tau = 1 / k_{\text{off}} / 60$ (minutes)
is calculated and displayed. A longer residence time generally supports more complete
lysosomal payload delivery.

## Sub-tab B: Epitope Characterization

### Inputs

Provide a description of the epitope region (e.g.\ "Domain IV of HER2 ECD"), select the
epitope type (Linear / Conformational / Glycan-dependent), and indicate whether binding
is conformation-sensitive.

### Outputs

| Output | Description |
|---|---|
| Epitope type | Linear, Conformational, or Glycan-dependent |
| Accessibility note | Assay implications; denaturation sensitivity |
| Cross-reactivity risk | Probability of binding sequence homologs |
| ADC relevance | Epitope stability under lysosomal trafficking |

## Sub-tab C: FcRn / Half-Life Prediction

### Background

Neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding at pH 6.0 in endosomes rescues IgG from lysosomal
degradation and recycles it to the cell surface, extending serum half-life. Fc engineering
mutations increase FcRn affinity and prolong half-life. ADC payload conjugation reduces
half-life due to increased hydrophobicity and accelerated clearance.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Options |
|---|---|
| IgG subclass | IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, IgG4 |
| Fc mutations | YTE (M252Y/S254T/T256E); LS (M428L/N434S); M428L/N434S; GASDALIE; N434H; none |
| DAR | 1--8 |
| Conjugation site | Cys-engineered; Lys (NHS ester); Fab-Cys; Fc-glycan; N-term |

### Prediction model

$$t_{1/2,\text{predicted}} = t_{1/2,\text{base}} \times \prod_i f_i \times (1 - p_{\text{DAR}} - p_{\text{site}})$$

where $f_i$ is the fold-change for each Fc mutation, $p_{\text{DAR}}$ is the DAR-dependent
clearance penalty (5\%--35\%), and $p_{\text{site}}$ is the conjugation-site penalty (0--10\%).

**Fc mutation effects used in model:**

| Mutation | Fold change | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| YTE (M252Y/S254T/T256E) | 1.50 | Increased FcRn pH 6.0 affinity; faster recycling |
| LS (M428L/N434S) | 1.30 | FcRn affinity enhancement |
| M428L/N434S | 1.50 | Same residue pair as LS; equivalent effect |
| GASDALIE | 0.67 | Enhanced FcγRIII for ADCC; slightly faster clearance |
| N434H | 1.30 | Moderate FcRn improvement |

**IgG subclass baselines:** IgG1 = 21 d; IgG2 = 20 d; IgG3 = 7 d; IgG4 = 21 d.

### Outputs

- Predicted half-life (days) with 85--115\% uncertainty range.
- Half-life tier badge (Excellent $\geq 25$ d / Good 18--25 d / Moderate 10--18 d / Short $< 10$ d).
- Calculation breakdown with base value, mutation multiplier, DAR penalty, site penalty.
- Bar chart comparing IgG1 wild-type baseline, subclass baseline, post-mutation, and
  final predicted ADC half-life.

# Tab 11 --- PK \& Efficacy (new in v1.0)

Tab 11 provides two pharmacology tools for understanding ADC systemic behaviour.

## Sub-tab A: Bystander Effect Scorer

### Background

Bystander killing refers to the ability of a cell-permeable payload, released from an
antigen-positive cell, to diffuse into and kill adjacent antigen-negative cells.
This is therapeutically important in antigen-heterogeneous tumors where not every
tumor cell expresses the target antigen at sufficient density for direct ADC binding.

### Scoring

The bystander score is a composite 0--8 scale:

| Component | Weight | Criterion |
|---|---|---|
| Cell permeability | +5 | Payload is cell-permeable (True / False) |
| Potency contribution | +3 / +1 / +0 | IC\textsubscript{50} $< 1$ nM / 1--10 nM / $> 10$ nM |

Scores 7--8 = High bystander; 4--6 = Moderate; 0--3 = Low.

**Clinical implication:** Payloads with High bystander score (MMAE, DXd, SN-38) are
preferred for solid tumor ADCs where antigen heterogeneity is expected. Low-bystander
payloads (DM1, DM4, MMAF, calicheamicin) require high uniform antigen density.

## Sub-tab B: PK Simulation

### Model

A one-compartment open pharmacokinetic model is applied:

$$C_{\text{intact}}(t) = C_0 \cdot e^{-k_e t}$$

$$C_{\text{naked}}(t) = C_0 \cdot \frac{k_{\text{deconj}}}{k_{\text{deconj}} - k_e} \cdot \left( e^{-k_e t} - e^{-k_{\text{deconj}} t} \right)$$

where $k_e = \ln(2) / t_{1/2,\text{ADC}}$ and $k_{\text{deconj}} = \ln(2) / t_{1/2,\text{deconj}}$.
$C_0$ is estimated from dose and a fixed distribution volume of $V_d = 3.5$ L/kg
(standard IgG assumption).

### Inputs

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Dose (mg/kg) | Administered dose |
| Antibody half-life (days) | From FcRn predictor (Tab 10) or literature |
| DAR | Drug-to-antibody ratio |
| Deconjugation t\textsubscript{1/2} (days) | From deconjugation predictor (Tab 8) |
| Simulation period (days) | 7--42 |

### Outputs

- Dual-curve concentration-time plot: teal solid line (intact ADC), grey dashed line
  (deconjugated / naked antibody).
- Peak concentration (C\textsubscript{max}) of intact ADC.
- Area under the curve (AUC) of intact ADC over the simulation period
  (trapezoidal rule, $\mu$g$\cdot$d/mL).
- Downloadable PK table as CSV.

\begin{notebox}
\textbf{Interpretation note:} This is a simplified single-compartment model for
rapid design-stage estimation. It does not account for two-compartment distribution,
receptor-mediated clearance, target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD), or inter-individual
variability. For regulatory submissions, full population PK modelling is required.
\end{notebox}

# Tab 12 --- AI Assistant

The AI Assistant provides a conversational interface to three LLM providers, pre-configured
with ADC peptide mapping and drug design context.

## Provider Selection

Three providers are supported:

| Provider | Model examples | Key type |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic (Claude) | claude-opus-4, claude-sonnet-5 | sk-ant- |
| OpenAI (GPT) | gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo | sk- |
| Google Gemini | gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-2.0-flash | AIza |

The available model list is populated dynamically from the selected provider's API.

## Rate Limiting

When no server-side key is set (shinyapps.io public deployment), a session limit of 10
messages is enforced. The usage counter is displayed with colour-coded status
(green: $\geq 4$ messages remaining; amber: 1--3 remaining; red: limit reached).
Providing your own API key removes the session limit.

## Context Injection

Enable **Include digest context** to automatically append the current ADC name, chain
count, enzyme, missed cleavage setting, and peptide count to each message. This
allows the model to give experiment-specific advice without manual copy-paste.

## Example questions for ADC design guidance

- *"Which of my linker options would give the best plasma stability for a HER2-targeting ADC?"*
- *"My deconjugation model shows DAR dropping below 1.4 by day 7 --- what linker change would extend this?"*
- *"For a target with internalization score of 6, would a PBD dimer or MMAE be more appropriate?"*
- *"My FcRn predictor gives 12 days half-life. What Fc mutation would get me to 20+ days?"*
- *"Explain why MMAF is preferred over MMAE when bystander killing is not desired."*

# Deployment to shinyapps.io

The v1.0 application, including all four new ADC design modules, deploys to shinyapps.io
without modification. All prediction logic is pure R with no binary dependencies.

```r
install.packages('rsconnect')
rsconnect::setAccountInfo(
  name   = 'your-account-name',
  token  = 'YOUR_TOKEN',
  secret = 'YOUR_SECRET'
)
source('deploy.R')
```

After deploying, set environment variables in the shinyapps.io dashboard:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = sk-ant-...   # optional
OPENAI_API_KEY    = sk-...       # optional
GEMINI_API_KEY    = AIza...      # optional
```

At least one key must be set server-side to remove the 10-message session limit for
public users.

Unit tests and mass accuracy benchmarks are unchanged from v0.8:

```r
setwd('path/to/ADC_Peptide_Mapper_v1.0')
source('R/digest.R')
source('R/modifications.R')
source('R/transitions.R')
source('R/isotopes.R')
source('R/dar.R')
source('tests/test_masses.R')              # 79 tests
source('tests/benchmark_mass_accuracy.R') # 10 reference peptides
```

Expected output: `79 / 79 PASSED` and `10 / 10 PASSED`.

No new formal unit tests are included for the v1.0 design modules in this release,
as all four modules use curated lookup tables and deterministic rule-based functions
that are verified by inspection. A test suite for these modules is planned for v1.1.

# Scientific Background

## Mass Calculation and Fragment Ions

Unchanged from v0.8. All masses are monoisotopic. Peptide mass:

$$M_{\text{neutral}} = \sum_{i} m_{r_i} + 18.010565 + \sum_{j} \Delta m_j$$

Precursor m/z: $m/z = (M_{\text{neutral}} + z \times 1.007276) / z$.

b-ions: N-terminal fragments (b2 through b$(n-1)$); y-ions: C-terminal fragments
+ H\textsubscript{2}O (y2 through y$(n-1)$). All product ions singly charged.

## Deconjugation Model

First-order decay with chemistry-specific rate constant:

$$k_e = \frac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}}$$

The sub-therapeutic DAR threshold is set at 35\% of the initial DAR, reflecting the
approximate point below which in-vivo efficacy is substantially reduced for most
auristatin- and maytansinoid-based ADCs (Shen 2012; Lyon 2015).

## FcRn Half-Life Prediction

The model uses published Fc mutation fold-change data from Dall'Acqua et al.\ (2006)
for YTE, from Zalevsky et al.\ (2010) and Shields et al.\ (2001) for LS/M428L--N434S,
and from Lazar et al.\ (2006) for GASDALIE. DAR and conjugation-site penalties are
derived from published ADC PK data (Hamblett et al.\ 2004; Shen et al.\ 2012).

## Internalization Database

Target internalization scores are curated from peer-reviewed ADC preclinical and clinical
data. Receptor class assignments follow GO Cellular Component and UniProt topology
annotations. Scores reflect the rate and completeness of endosomal trafficking, not surface
expression level.

## Bystander Scoring

Cell permeability classification is derived from published ADC bystander studies
(Li et al.\ 2016; Ogitani et al.\ 2016; Staudacher \& Hartley 2018). IC\textsubscript{50}
values are in-vitro cytotoxicity data from published sources; they represent free payload
potency, not ADC-level potency.

# Troubleshooting

## App does not launch

- Confirm all required packages are installed (`shiny`, `bs4Dash`, `DT`, `data.table`,
  `openxlsx`, `httr2`, `stringr`, `dplyr`, `shinyjs`, `htmltools`).
- Check that `data/bg_human.rds` exists; run `source('build_background_db.R')` if not.

## New design modules show no output

- The deconjugation predictor, internalization scorer, surface accessibility assessor,
  binding affinity scorer, epitope characterizer, half-life predictor, bystander scorer,
  and PK simulator all require clicking the respective action button after setting inputs.
  No output appears until the button is clicked.
- The payload comparison panel requires selecting two payload names from the dropdowns
  before clicking **Compare**.

## Target not found in internalization or surface database

- The databases cover 40 (internalization) and 27 (surface) targets. Partial matching is
  applied (e.g.\ entering ``HER'' matches the first result containing that substring).
- For targets not in the database, consult internalization assay literature and enter a
  KD-based affinity score manually in Tab 10.

## AI Assistant returns API error

- Verify the API key prefix matches the selected provider (sk-ant- for Anthropic,
  sk- for OpenAI, AIza for Gemini).
- Confirm internet access: `httr2::request('https://api.anthropic.com') |> httr2::req_perform()`
- If the model dropdown is empty, the key may be invalid or the provider API is temporarily
  unavailable.

## MS Amanda not detected (Tab 6)

- See the v0.8 User Manual Section 8 for detailed platform-specific instructions.
- Set `MSAMANDA_EXE` in `~/.Renviron` and restart R.

## shinyapps.io deployment bundle too large

- Edit `INCLUDE_SPECIES` in `deploy.R` to exclude background species not required.
- Exclude `tests/` and large local files via `EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` in `deploy.R`.
